comments.text:
C++'s ABI compatibility guarantees exist *because* so many companies "fired all the engineers" in the 90s after finishing their product and literally do not have the source code to their compiled binaries, yet still need to add more functionality. I can call directly into a binary compiled in the 90s and things still work (except std::string but we don't talk about that).

It's inefficient in practice which is why modern languages don't make these guarantees, but it exists and you can be employed to deal with it.
